question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.
Makeshift
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Provisional.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Makeshift" means a temporary substitute or arrangement used until something more permanent or better is available, i.e., something provisional in nature. (अस्थायी)
◦ Example: They used a wooden plank as a makeshift bridge until the real one was repaired.

• "Provisional" means arranged or existing for the present, possibly to be changed later; temporary. (अस्थायी) This closely matches the meaning of "makeshift".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Resourceful" (साधन संपन्न): Having the ability to find quick and clever ways to overcome difficulties.

• Option 3: "Perpetual" (चिरस्थायी): Never ending or changing; continuing forever — this is actually the opposite of "makeshift".

• Option 4: "Inconsiderate" (विचारहीन): Thoughtlessly causing hurt or inconvenience to others.

NOTE

• Synonyms of "Makeshift" commonly asked in SSC: temporary, stopgap, expedient, improvised.

• Do not confuse "makeshift" (temporary arrangement) with "perpetual" or "permanent" (lasting forever) — these are antonyms, not synonyms.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word from the following sentence.
Ambitious
He aspires to be a future diplomat but he will have to improve his decision-making skills.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. aspires.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Ambitious" means having a strong desire to achieve success, power, or distinction; full of ambition. (महत्वाकांक्षी)

• "Aspires" (from the verb "aspire") means to have a strong desire to achieve something high or great. (आकांक्षा रखना) This is closest in meaning to "ambitious", since a person who aspires to something is driven by ambition.
◦ Example: She aspires to become a successful entrepreneur one day.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "Improve" means to make or become better — it does not relate to having a strong desire for success.

• Option 3: "Decision" means a conclusion reached after consideration — unrelated to ambition.

• Option 4: "Skills" means the ability to do something well — unrelated to ambition.

NOTE

• Related words: ambition (noun) — aspiration, aim, goal, drive, zeal.

• "Aspire" is always followed by "to" (aspire to be/do something), e.g., "He aspires to be a doctor."

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined word in the given sentence.
The fall of Ranjith for the petty material benefit was really ignominious.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. reprehensible.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Ignominious" means deserving or causing public disgrace or shame; humiliating. (अपमानजनक/शर्मनाक)

• "Reprehensible" means deserving strong criticism or censure; blameworthy. (निंदनीय) This is the closest match, since Ranjith's fall for petty material benefit is being condemned as shameful and blameworthy conduct.
◦ Example: His reprehensible behaviour at the party embarrassed the entire family.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Unfaltering" means steady and not weakening — the opposite sense, not fitting a disgraceful fall.

• Option 2: "Amusing" means causing laughter or entertainment — unrelated to disgrace.

• Option 4: "Ignorable" means able to be ignored or disregarded — this does not capture the sense of shame/disgrace conveyed by "ignominious".

NOTE

• Do not confuse "ignominious" (shameful) with "ignorable" (able to be overlooked) — despite the similar spelling, their meanings are very different.

• Other synonyms of "ignominious": disgraceful, humiliating, shameful, dishonourable.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the underlined group of words.
WHO is an organisation that raises money for a particular cause.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. fundraiser.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "Fundraiser" is defined as an organisation, event, or campaign whose purpose is to collect/raise money for a particular cause. (धन एकत्र करने वाला संगठन/अभियान) This matches the underlined phrase exactly, since WHO (World Health Organization) works to raise resources and support for global health causes.
◦ Example: The charity marathon was organised as a fundraiser for cancer research.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Donation" (दान): A gift, usually of money, given to a cause or organisation — it refers to the money given, not to the organisation itself.

• Option 2: "Volunteer" (स्वयंसेवक): A person who freely offers to do a task without being paid — refers to a person, not an organisation.

• Option 3: "Charity" (दान संस्था): An organisation set up specifically to help people in need (e.g. the poor or sick) — it is narrower than "an organisation that raises money for a particular cause", which can include causes other than helping the needy.

NOTE

• Related one-word substitutions often asked in SSC: philanthropist (a person who donates generously to good causes), benefactor (a person who gives financial help), almoner (a person who distributes charity).

• "Fundraiser" can refer both to the organising body/event and, informally, to a person tasked with raising funds.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined words in the given sentence.
The new restaurant is more better than the old one.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. better.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Better" is already the comparative degree of the adjective "good". Comparative adjectives must never be preceded by another comparative marker such as "more".

• Rule — Degrees of Comparison:
◦ Positive: good
◦ Comparative: better (not "more better")
◦ Superlative: best (not "most best")

• Since only two things are being compared — "the new restaurant" and "the old one" — the comparative degree "better" alone is required.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Most better" is incorrect because "most" (a superlative marker) cannot combine with "better" (a comparative form) — this is a mismatched double comparison.

• Option 3: "Much more better" is incorrect for the same reason — it doubles up two comparative markers ("more" and the already-comparative "better").

• Option 4: "The best" is incorrect because "best" is the superlative degree, used only when comparing three or more things, not two.

NOTE

• Irregular comparative/superlative forms frequently tested by SSC: good – better – best, bad – worse – worst, little – less – least, many/much – more – most.

• Never use "more" or "most" with an adjective that is already in its comparative or superlative form (e.g., avoid "more better", "most best", "more easier").

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.
The teacher did not allow the students to leave the lecture.
option_1: The students are not allowed to leave the lecture.
option_2: The students had not been allowed to leave the lecture by the teacher.
option_3: The students had not allowed the teacher to leave the lecture.
option_4: The students were not allowed to leave the lecture by the teacher.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. The students were not allowed to leave the lecture by the teacher.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence "The teacher did not allow the students to leave the lecture" is a negative sentence in the Simple Past Tense.

• Rule — Simple Past Tense:
◦ Active: Subject + did not + V1 + Object
◦ Passive: Object + was/were + not + V3 + by + Subject

• Applying the rule: the object "the students" becomes the subject; being plural, it takes "were"; the verb "allow" becomes the past participle "allowed"; and "the teacher" becomes the agent introduced by "by".
◦ Passive: The students were not allowed to leave the lecture by the teacher.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is incorrect because "are not allowed" is in the Simple Present Tense, but the original sentence is in the Simple Past Tense; it also drops the agent "by the teacher".

• Option 2 is incorrect because "had not been allowed" is the Past Perfect passive form, which changes the tense of the original sentence.

• Option 3 is incorrect because the subject and object have been wrongly interchanged, giving the illogical meaning that the students did not allow the teacher to leave.

NOTE

• When a sentence contains an infinitive construction like "allow someone to do something", only the main verb (allow) is converted into the passive form; the infinitive "to leave" remains unchanged.

• Similar structures: permit, order, ask, tell + object + infinitive, e.g., "He ordered the soldiers to retreat" → "The soldiers were ordered to retreat by him."

question:
Select the most appropriate idiom for the underlined segment in the following sentence.
The servants know the secrets of the family they are working for.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Ins and outs.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "Ins and outs" means all the details and complexities of something, including its secrets. (सभी बारीकियां/रहस्य) It exactly captures the meaning of "secrets" in the given sentence.
◦ Example: After years of working there, she knew the ins and outs of the company.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: To be Greek to someone / Latin and Greek (समझ में न आना): Used for something unintelligible or hard to understand — it does not mean "secrets".

• Option 3: To stir/disturb a hornet's nest (मुसीबत मोल लेना): To do something that provokes trouble or widespread anger — unrelated to knowing secrets.

• Option 4: The long and short (सारांश) of something: The basic facts or the summary of a matter, without going into detail — this means the gist, not the secrets.

NOTE

• Other idioms of knowledge/secrecy often asked in SSC: "To be in the know" (to have inside information), "Behind closed doors" (privately/secretly), "To let the cat out of the bag" (to reveal a secret).

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
Washington Irving’s writing career started at / the tender age of nineteen when he joined / his brother Peter’s newspaper The Morning Chronical / as journalist.
option_1: his brother Peter’s newspaper The Morning Chronical
option_2: Washington Irving’s writing career started at
option_4: the tender age of nineteen when he joined
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. as journalist.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The segment "as journalist" is grammatically incorrect because the singular countable noun "journalist" must be preceded by the indefinite article "a".

• Rule — Use of Articles: A singular, countable common noun (like "journalist", "teacher", "doctor") must always take an article (a/an/the) before it, unless it is used in a special idiomatic sense.

• Corrected segment: "as a journalist".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "his brother Peter's newspaper The Morning Chronical" — grammatically correct; the possessive form and the naming of the newspaper are properly constructed.

• Option 2: "Washington Irving's writing career started at" — grammatically correct; correct possessive and verb form.

• Option 4: "the tender age of nineteen when he joined" — grammatically correct; correct preposition and relative structure.

NOTE

• A missing article before a singular countable noun (especially after "as", "of", "for") is one of the most frequently tested error types in SSC exams.

• Similarly tested phrases: "worked as a manager", "appointed as a director", "served as a soldier" — never drop the article "a/an" here.

question:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.
A. Isabel saw a strange rabbit running through the bushes.
B. Following it, she found a door which she opened with the help of keys.
C. After that, she felt a strange sensation in her body.
D. She thought as if she was in a dream.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. ABCD.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Sentence A introduces the event that starts the story — Isabel seeing a strange rabbit — and must come first, since every other sentence refers back to it using the pronoun "it".

• Sentence B logically follows A, as "Following it" refers directly back to the rabbit in sentence A, describing how she found and opened a door.

• Sentence C follows B, as "After that" refers to the action of opening the door, describing the strange sensation that resulted.

• Sentence D comes last, as it describes her resulting thought/feeling ("as if she was in a dream") after already feeling the strange sensation described in C.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4 (ABCD).

Additional Information

• Option 1 (CDAB) is incorrect because it begins with "After that", which has no preceding event to refer to.

• Option 2 (DCAB) is incorrect because it begins with her thought/feeling before the rabbit or the door has even been introduced.

• Option 3 (BCDA) is incorrect because it begins with "Following it", but the rabbit ("it") has not yet been mentioned.

NOTE

• In para-jumble questions, always locate the independent, self-contained sentence (one with no pronoun referring back to something unstated) — that sentence is almost always the opening sentence.

• Pay close attention to linking words/pronouns such as "it", "this", "that", "following", "after that" — they always point back to information given in an earlier sentence.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word in brackets to fill in the blank.
After the rain stopped, the air smelled fresh and clean, and the sun ________________ (stared) out from behind the clouds.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. peeked.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Stared" means to look fixedly or intently at something for a long time. (घूरना)

• "Peeked" means to look quickly and often furtively at something, a brief or partial glance. (झांकना) This is opposite in intensity/duration to a fixed, prolonged "stare", making it the correct antonym in this context.
◦ Example: The child peeked out from behind the curtain to see who had arrived.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "Observed" (देखना/निरीक्षण करना): To watch or notice carefully — similar in intensity to "stared", not opposite.

• Option 3: "Spied" (जासूसी करना/छिपकर देखना): To watch secretly, often for a specific purpose — again a watchful, attentive look, not opposite to "stared".

• Option 4: "Surveyed" (सर्वेक्षण करना): To look carefully or thoroughly over something, often to assess it — also close to "stared" in intensity, not its opposite.

NOTE

• Remember: an antonym of "stare" (a long, fixed look) is a brief, quick look — words like peek, glance, glimpse.

• Common SSC antonym-in-context questions test the ability to distinguish near-synonyms (observed, spied, surveyed) from the true opposite (peeked) based on duration/intensity of the action, not just literal meaning.

question:
Select the most appropriate homophone to fill in the blank.
Developers ____________ the old buildings on the site to make way for new construction.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. raze.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Raze" means to completely destroy or demolish a building or town, which fits the context of developers clearing old buildings to make way for new construction.
◦ Example: The old cinema hall was razed to build a shopping mall.

• Rule — Homophones: Homophones are words that sound alike but differ in spelling and meaning. Here, "raze", "rays", "raise" and "rase" are pronounced similarly but only "raze" fits the meaning of "demolish".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "Rays" refers to narrow beams of light (or other radiation) — unrelated to demolishing buildings.

• Option 3: "Raise" means to lift up or increase something (e.g., raise a building, raise funds) — this is the opposite of destroying a structure, so it doesn't fit the context of clearing old buildings.

• Option 4: "Rase" is a rare/archaic spelling variant of "raze" that is not used in standard modern English; it is not the conventionally accepted spelling.

NOTE

• Commonly confused homophones tested by SSC: raze/raise/rays, principal/principle, stationary/stationery, complement/compliment, affect/effect.

• Remember the mnemonic: "raZe" has a Z like "demoliZe" (destroy), while "raIse" has an I like "lIft".

question:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.
(A) The new movie was highly anticipated by fans of the franchise.
(B) As the lights dimmed, the audience grew quiet in anticipation.
(C) The movie began with an exciting action sequence that had the audience on the edge of their seats.
(D) The movie theatre was packed with people eager to see it.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. ADBC.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Sentence A ("The new movie was highly anticipated by fans of the franchise.") is the best opening sentence — it introduces the movie and the general excitement surrounding it before any scene-specific details are given.

• Sentence D follows A, as it narrows the anticipation down to a concrete scene: the theatre being packed with eager viewers.

• Sentence B follows D, describing the next chronological event — the lights dimming and the audience falling silent in anticipation, just before the movie starts.

• Sentence C comes last, describing the movie actually beginning with an exciting action sequence — the natural conclusion of the build-up described in A, D and B.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3 (ADBC).

Additional Information

• Option 1 (CBDA) is incorrect because it starts with the movie already beginning (C), before the build-up (anticipation, packed theatre, dimming lights) has been described.

• Option 2 (BCDA) is incorrect because it has the lights dimming and the movie starting before the theatre is even described as packed.

• Option 4 (DBAC) is incorrect because it separates the general anticipation of fans (A) from the packed theatre (D), disturbing the natural flow from general excitement to a specific scene.

NOTE

• In paragraph-jumble questions, look for a general, scene-setting sentence to begin with, followed by increasingly specific, chronologically ordered details.

• Time-sequence indicator phrases like "As the lights dimmed" and "The movie began with" are strong clues to the correct chronological order.

question: Select the correctly spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Suspicion.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "Suspicion" — a feeling or thought that something is possible, likely, or true, especially something bad or wrong, without proof.
◦ Example: The police arrested him on suspicion of theft.

• Spelling key: SUS + PIC + ION. Note there is only a single "s" after "sus" and a single "p" before "icion" — a common error is doubling one of these consonants.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "Susspicion" — incorrect; an extra "s" has been wrongly added after "sus".

• Option 3: "Susppicion" — incorrect; an extra "p" has been wrongly added before "icion".

• Option 4: "Suspicon" — incorrect; the "i" before the final "on" has been dropped, it should be "-icion" not "-icon".

NOTE

• The related adjective is suspicious, and the related verb is suspect.

• Other commonly misspelt "-cion/-tion/-sion" words in SSC: coercion, decision, occasion, permission, discussion.

question:
Select the most appropriate idiom for the underlined segment in the following sentence.
Shruti is a strange person because of her attitude.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Queer fish.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "Queer fish" refers to a strange, eccentric, or unusual person. (अजीब/विचित्र व्यक्ति) This directly matches the underlined phrase "strange person" in the given sentence.
◦ Example: Nobody understands him fully; he has always been a queer fish.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "A one man" (referring to "a one-man show"): Used for an activity or organisation run and controlled entirely by a single person — unrelated to being strange.

• Option 2: "A scarlet woman" (कुलटा स्त्री): An old-fashioned, derogatory term for a woman considered sexually promiscuous — unrelated to the sentence's meaning.

• Option 4: "A straw man" (तर्कहीन विरोधी): A weak argument, or a person/argument set up only to be easily knocked down/refuted — unrelated to being strange.

NOTE

• Other idioms describing unusual people often asked in SSC: "an odd ball" (an eccentric person), "a dark horse" (someone with hidden talents/unknown qualities), "an eccentric" (a person with unconventional/strange habits).

question:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Select the option that arranges the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.
A) the importance
B) to be treated
C) of treating other people
D) now he knows
E) as he would like
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. D, A, C, E, B.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Part D ("now he knows") must come first, since it introduces the subject "he" and the main verb "knows", on which the rest of the sentence depends.

• Part A ("the importance") follows D, forming the object of "knows" — "now he knows the importance...".

• Part C ("of treating other people") follows A, since "importance" must be followed by "of + gerund" to specify what the importance relates to — "the importance of treating other people".

• Parts E ("as he would like") and B ("to be treated") come last, completing the comparison — "...as he would like to be treated", meaning he should treat others the way he wishes to be treated himself.

• Full sentence: "Now he knows the importance of treating other people as he would like to be treated."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1 (D, A, C, E, B).

Additional Information

• Option 2 (B, D, C, A, E) is incorrect because it begins with an infinitive phrase ("to be treated") that has no preceding context to attach to.

• Option 3 (C, D, B, A, E) is incorrect because it begins with "of treating other people", which cannot logically open the sentence without "the importance" first.

• Option 4 (C, E, B, A, D) is incorrect because it produces a grammatically broken, meaningless sequence with no clear subject-verb opening.

NOTE

• In jumbled-sentence questions, first identify the part containing the subject and main verb — it usually opens the sentence.

• Watch for phrases like "the importance of + gerund" and comparative structures with "as...would like to...", which must stay linked together in the correct sequence.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.
A form of government in which power is held by the nobility
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Aristocracy.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Aristocracy" means a form of government in which power is held by a small privileged ruling class, especially the nobility. (कुलीनतंत्र) This is an exact match for the given definition.
◦ Example: In the aristocracy of old Europe, land and titles were passed down through noble families.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Democracy" (लोकतंत्र): A form of government in which power is held by the people, exercised directly or through elected representatives — the opposite of rule by the nobility.

• Option 3: "Republic" (गणराज्य): A state in which supreme power is held by the people and their elected representatives, and which has an elected or nominated president rather than a monarch.

• Option 4: "Nobility" (कुलीन वर्ग): Refers to the privileged class itself (the people), not to the system/form of government they rule under.

NOTE

• Other forms-of-government one-word substitutes often asked in SSC: Monarchy (rule by a single king/queen), Oligarchy (rule by a small group of people), Theocracy (rule by religious leaders), Anarchy (absence of government/rule).

question:
Choose the correct meaning of the underlined word in the given sentence.
The World Health Organization has finally issued guidelines to prevent the spread of the Covid-19 epidemic.
option_1: A large number of people or animals suffering from the same disease at the same time
option_2: An infection which is caused by viruses
option_4: A disease which lasts for more than fifty years
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. A large number of people or animals suffering from the same disease at the same time.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Epidemic" means a widespread occurrence of an infectious disease affecting a large number of people or animals in a community or region at a particular time. (महामारी) This matches Option 1 exactly.
◦ Example: The flu epidemic of 1918 killed millions of people worldwide.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 is incorrect because an epidemic is not necessarily caused specifically by viruses — it can be caused by bacteria, viruses, or other infectious agents; the defining feature of "epidemic" is its widespread and rapid occurrence, not its cause.

• Option 3 is incorrect because an epidemic typically spreads rapidly, not slowly, among a population.

• Option 4 is incorrect because "epidemic" refers to how widely and quickly a disease spreads, not to how long it lasts.

NOTE

• Related words often confused with "epidemic": "Pandemic" (an epidemic that has spread across multiple countries/continents), "Endemic" (a disease regularly found in a particular area or population), "Outbreak" (a sudden rise in the occurrence of a disease in a specific place).

question:
Select the most appropriate option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.
The professor assigns the homework every week.
option_1: The homework is assigning by the professor every week.
option_2: The homework will be assigned by the professor every week.
option_3: The homework assigns by the professor every week.
option_4: The homework is assigned by the professor every week.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. The homework is assigned by the professor every week.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence "The professor assigns the homework every week" is an assertive sentence in the Simple Present Tense.

• Rule — Simple Present Tense:
◦ Active: Subject + V1/V5 + Object
◦ Passive: Object + is/am/are + V3 + by + Subject

• Applying the rule: the object "the homework" becomes the subject; being singular, it takes "is"; the verb "assigns" becomes the past participle "assigned"; and "the professor" becomes the agent with "by".
◦ Passive: The homework is assigned by the professor every week.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is incorrect because "is assigning" is a present continuous form, not the correct passive construction (which requires "is + V3", not "is + V-ing").

• Option 2 is incorrect because "will be assigned" is the passive of the Simple Future Tense, changing the tense of the original sentence.

• Option 3 is incorrect because it uses the active verb form "assigns" instead of the passive auxiliary + past participle structure ("is assigned").

NOTE

• A common trap in passive-voice questions is confusing present continuous ("is/are + V-ing") with the passive marker "is/are + V3" — always check that the verb is in its past participle form, not the "-ing" form.

• The frequency adverb "every week" stays in the same position (usually at the end) in both active and passive versions.

question:
Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
The Special Task Force will conduct a thorough probe in the land scam case which has Mr. Lakhan Lal as the prime akused.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Akused.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "Accused", not "Akused" — meaning a person charged with or on trial for a crime.
◦ Example: The accused was produced before the court for the hearing.

• Spelling key: AC + CUSE + D. The word begins with "ac-" (not "ak-") and contains a double "c" — "accuse" — before adding "-d".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Scam" is correctly spelt; it means a dishonest scheme or fraud.

• Option 2: "Prime" is correctly spelt; it means of first importance or main.

• Option 3: "Thorough" is correctly spelt; it means complete and carried out with great attention to detail.

NOTE

• Do not confuse the letter "k" for "c" — words of Latin origin such as accuse, accurate, accompany, accident always use "cc", never "kk" or "k".

• Related words: accusation (noun), accusatory (adjective), accuser (noun).

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM to substitute the underlined word in the given sentence.
The newly selected secretary of the party has a/an impeccable image among the public.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Blemished.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Impeccable" means flawless, faultless, or in accordance with the highest standards; without any blemish. (त्रुटिहीन/निष्कलंक)

• "Blemished" means marked or spoiled by a flaw or imperfection. (दाग़दार/दोषयुक्त) This is the direct opposite of "impeccable", making it the correct antonym.
◦ Example: His blemished record made it difficult for him to win the public's trust.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Refurbished" (नवीनीकृत): Cleaned up and renovated, especially of a building or a used product — unrelated to a person's reputation.

• Option 3: "Irresistible" (अनूठा/जिसका विरोध न हो सके): Too attractive or convincing to be resisted — not opposite in meaning to "impeccable".

• Option 4: "Arbitrary" (मनमाना): Based on random choice or personal whim rather than reason or system — unrelated to the meaning of "impeccable".

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "impeccable": flawless, immaculate, spotless, perfect.

• Other antonyms of "impeccable": flawed, defective, imperfect, tarnished.

Comprehension:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Upgrading the higher education sector especially in terms of patents filed and cutting-edge research output is (1)________ in improving India’s global ranking. Our sustainable (2)________ development depends on human resources. A quality higher education base is essential to reap the full benefits of our demographic dividend. In higher education, the strategies of the 12th plan (3)________ on technical education, distance learning, quality research, infrastructure, faculty, and curriculum content. (4)________ efforts of the government departments and the private sector are needed to (5)________ the plan’s educational goals.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. essential.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank requires a word that logically completes: **"Upgrading the higher education sector...is ________ in improving India's global ranking."** The sentence is emphasizing the necessity of this factor for improving the ranking.

• "Essential" means absolutely necessary; extremely important. This fits the context perfectly, as the passage stresses that upgrading higher education is a necessary requirement for improving India's global ranking.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Unrequired" means not needed — this is the opposite of what the context demands, since the passage is stressing importance, not the lack of it.

• Option 2: "Deserving" means worthy of something — it does not fit grammatically or logically in this context ("is deserving in improving" is not idiomatic usage).

• Option 3: "Fulfilling" means satisfying or rewarding, or (as a participle) "carrying out" — it does not logically fit the sense of importance/necessity required here.

NOTE

• In cloze passages, always read the full sentence (and often the surrounding sentences) to identify the overall tone/theme before choosing a word — here, the theme of "necessity for improvement" points clearly to "essential".

• Words expressing necessity often tested by SSC: essential, indispensable, imperative, vital, crucial.

solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. social.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank appears in: **"Our sustainable ________ development depends on human resources." The passage is discussing overall national development that depends on people (human resources), which points to social development** — development connected with society and its people/human resources — as the most fitting term in this context.

• "Social development" refers to the process of improving the well-being, skills and welfare of people/society as a whole, and it is commonly linked in policy writing with the phrase "depends on human resources".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "Economic" relates to the production and management of wealth; while plausible, the passage's emphasis here is on human resources and welfare, which is better captured by "social" in this context.

• Option 3: "Psychological" relates to the mind and mental processes — it does not fit the context of national/educational development discussed in the passage.

• Option 4: "Political" relates to government and public affairs — it does not fit the context of development driven by human resources.

NOTE

• Cloze passages on national development frequently pair the word "sustainable" with "social", "economic", or "environmental" development — always use the surrounding context (here, "depends on human resources") to pick the most precise fit rather than the most common collocation.

• Related terms: human capital, human resource development (HRD), demographic dividend — all mentioned or implied elsewhere in this very passage.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. focus.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank appears in: **"...the strategies of the 12th plan ________ on technical education, distance learning, quality research, infrastructure, faculty, and curriculum content."**

• "Focus on" is the correct and idiomatic collocation meaning to concentrate attention or effort on a particular area. This fits perfectly, as the sentence lists several specific areas that the 12th plan's strategies concentrate on.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Understand" does not take the preposition "on" in this sense and does not fit the idea of strategies being directed at specific areas.

• Option 2: "Attend" normally collocates with "to" (attend to something), not "on"; it also does not carry the sense of strategic concentration required here.

• Option 3: "Divert" means to turn something away from its original course — this contradicts the sense of the sentence, which is about strategies being concentrated on these areas, not diverted from them.

NOTE

• "Focus on" and "concentrate on" are common fixed prepositional collocations frequently tested in SSC cloze passages.

• Be careful with verb-preposition pairings: attend to, focus on, dwell on, insist on, rely on — the correct preposition often determines the correct verb choice in cloze tests.

solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Coordinated.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank appears in: **"________ efforts of the government departments and the private sector are needed to realise the plan's educational goals."**

• "Coordinated efforts" is a standard fixed collocation meaning efforts that are organised and worked together in a well-planned, cooperative manner between different parties — here, between government departments and the private sector.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Sustained" means continued or maintained over a long period — it does not capture the sense of different parties (government departments and private sector) working together, which the sentence clearly requires.

• Option 2: "Compromised" means weakened or made to accept lower standards — this does not fit the positive sense of joint effort needed to achieve educational goals.

• Option 4: "Gathered" means collected or assembled — it does not naturally collocate with "efforts" in this cooperative sense.

NOTE

• "Coordinated efforts", "joint efforts", and "concerted efforts" are common fixed collocations tested in SSC cloze passages, all describing cooperative action between multiple parties.

• Watch for context clues like "government departments AND the private sector" — the word "and" signals a need for cooperation, pointing directly to "coordinated".

solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. realise.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank appears in: **"...are needed to ________ the plan's educational goals."**

• "Realise" (British spelling of "realize") means to achieve or bring something into being; to accomplish a plan, goal, or ambition. This is precisely the meaning required — coordinated efforts are needed to achieve/accomplish the plan's educational goals.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Remain" means to stay in the same place/state — it does not fit with "goals" as its object; one cannot "remain" a goal.

• Option 3: "Conclude" means to bring to an end or to deduce something — it does not fit the sense of actively achieving a goal.

• Option 4: "Conduct" means to organise or carry out an activity (e.g., conduct a survey/experiment) — it does not collocate naturally with "goals" in the sense of achieving them.

NOTE

• "Realise a goal/dream/ambition" is a standard fixed collocation frequently tested in SSC cloze passages, meaning to successfully achieve it.

• Since this is an Indian (SSC) English paper, the British spelling "realise" (rather than the American "realize") is used, consistent with the paper's overall British English convention.
